newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Polls show strong support for Australia's Hanson.
newsitem.headline: Polls show strong support for Australia's Hanson.

text.p: More than a third of Australians think right-wing populist Pauline Hanson's new political push is good for the country and the government should consider some of her controversial policies, a new poll showed on Thursday.

While 57 percent of Australians think Hanson's One Nation Party is bad for Australia, 35 percent think it is good. Thirty-nine percent feel Prime Minister John Howard should consider her ideas and listen to why people support her, said the Bulletin newsweekly's Morgan poll.
But 64 percent of those surveyed said the outspoken independent from Queensland state was inciting racial tension, while 33 percent disagreed.
Hanson's popularity has surged over recent weeks while that of Howard's Liberal-National coalition has plunged to its lowest since its landslide election win over Labor in March 1996.
A series of polls have shown voters are deserting Howard and moving to One Nation, which now ranks as the third political force in most polls, ahead of the left-leaning Australian Democrats.

The Reuters Poll Trend, which smoothes the volatility in the main published polls, shows the government's once-commanding lead over Labor has dropped from 12 percentage points over most of its term to barely six points.
Most of that fall has happened since Hanson's party was officially launched several weeks ago.

Hanson sparked a divisive national race row last year when she said Australia was at risk of being swamped by Asians and that Aborigines received government handouts and preferential treatment at the expense of white Australians.
One Nation's political rallies around the country have drawn thousands of supporters, but also sparked violent protests.
One Nation opposes immigration, foreign investment and Aboriginal welfare.
The Bulletin poll surveyed 1,021 voters face-to-face around the country on April 26 and 27.
